summary.title: About Project Euler
summary.one_liner: Project Euler is a series of challenging math and programming problems that need both mathematical insight and code to solve.
takeaways: Project Euler is a set of mathematical problems that require a computer and programming skills to solve, not just pen-and-paper maths.
Problems are meant to be solved progressively: each solved problem can expose a concept that unlocks harder ones (inductive chain learning).
The intended audience includes students, adults with an interest in mathematics, and professionals wanting to sharpen problem solving.
An account (free to register) is needed to track progress, and cookies must be enabled; problems can be viewed before registering.
The site reports 151216 registered members who have solved at least 25 problems, using 114 programming languages.
summary.summary: The About page describes Project Euler as a site of challenging maths and programming problems meant to be solved with code as well as mathematical insight. It explains the aim of encouraging learning new concepts in a recreational setting, and who the problems suit: students, adults with a maths interest, and professionals. It also covers how difficulty builds through chained learning, and how to register to track progress. The page gives no specific problem list or technical content beyond these points.
